## Statement

Assume AC. Let $F$ be a compact smooth manifold without boundary, possibly disconnected and nonorientable. Let $h$ be a unitary bundle automorphism covering the identity of $F$, obtained from the action of a fixed element of a compact torus, and acting on all symbol bundles compatibly with their maps. Put $n=\dim F$ componentwise. For a compact-support symbol class $a$ on $T^*F$, its trace-weighted compact-support Chern character is

$$\operatorname{ch}_{h,c}(a)=\sum_{\lambda}\lambda\,\operatorname{ch}_c(a_\lambda)\in H_c^{\mathrm{even}}(T^*F;\mathbb C),$$

where $a_\lambda$ is its symbol class on the $\lambda$-eigenbundles of $h$. The sum is finite on each compact disk-bundle representative; it is extended linearly to virtual classes. Here $\operatorname{ch}_c$ is the relative topological Chern character, not the Chern character of the alternating bundle restricted to the zero section.

Fix the following cotangent orientation and Bott normalization. If $\theta=\sum_j\xi_jdx_j$ is the tautological one-form, orient $T^*F$ by $(d\theta)^n/n!$, namely by $d\xi_1\wedge dx_1\wedge\cdots\wedge d\xi_n\wedge dx_n$. The plane Bott class is the even-to-odd symbol $z:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ on the plane $z=x+i\xi$, with its relative-triple convention corresponding to $[\gamma]-1$ for the tautological Hopf line. Write $p_{F,!}:K_c^0(T^*F)\to\mathbb Z$ for the embedding construction: use this Bott Thom class on the doubled real normal bundle of an embedding $F\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^N$, extend by zero into $T^*\mathbb R^N$, and invert the same plane Bott external product on $T^*\mathbb R^N$. Its trace-weighted extension is $p_{F,!,h}(a)=\sum_\lambda\lambda p_{F,!}(a_\lambda)$. Then

$$p_{F,!,h}(a)=\int_{T^*F}\operatorname{ch}_{h,c}(a)\,\pi^*\operatorname{Td}(TF\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C).$$

For a degree-$2n$ compact-support cohomology class, the integral means its pairing with the relative fundamental class $[D_R(T^*F),S_R(T^*F)]$, using a radius $R$ containing its support in the disk interior, excision and the indicated orientation of the total space. Only the degree-$2n$ part is paired, and components are summed. This definition uses an orientation of the cotangent total space and requires no orientation of $F$.

The Todd class of a complex bundle with formal Chern roots $x_j$ means $\prod_j x_j/(1-e^{-x_j})$, expanded only through the dimension of the base. The integer construction is independent of the chosen embedding and tubular data.

In particular, let $M$ be a compact smooth torus manifold, $g$ a torus element, $F$ a component of $M^g$, $\nu$ its real normal bundle, and $i:T^*F\hookrightarrow T^*M$ the inclusion using an invariant metric. Put $e_g=\lambda_{-1}(\nu_{\mathbb C}^*)$ and let $\sigma\in K^0_{T,c}(T^*M)$ be any compact elliptic symbol class. The character of $e_g$ at $g$ is nonzero, and the trace-weighted Chern character extends to localization at virtual representations whose character at $g$ is nonzero. Whenever the representation-localized K-group supplies a class $b$ with $e_g b=i^*\sigma$ (in particular, the quotient $b=i^*\sigma/e_g$ furnished by K-localization), one has

$$p_{F,!,g}(b)=\int_{T^*F}\frac{\operatorname{ch}_{g,c}(i^*\sigma)}{\pi^*\operatorname{ch}_g(\lambda_{-1}(\nu_{\mathbb C}^*))}\,\pi^*\operatorname{Td}(TF_{\mathbb C}).$$

This is the characteristic-class comparison for a fixed component. It applies to the compact symbol of a general first-order elliptic complex after forming its even-to-odd elliptic symbol. It does not assert localization of equivariant K-theory or equality of analytic and topological indices; those are separate prerequisites for identifying the sum of these expressions with an analytic character. With the other common cotangent symplectic convention $-d\theta$, both displayed integrals acquire the factor $(-1)^n$.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** Compute the ordinary Thom Chern character on universal lines, descend by splitting, apply it to the doubled real normal of an embedding, and then take the trace on eigenbundles.

1.1 A compact symbol on a vector bundle over a compact base can be restricted to a closed disk containing its noninvertibility set and radially identified with the disk/sphere pair. Radial contraction of the disk onto its zero section and [F7] identify both bundles there with pullbacks of bundles on the compact base. Its relative K-class is obtained by clutching its two bundles along the sphere using the boundary isomorphism. To see this in the based-quotient model, double the disk, glue the first bundle on its positive half to the second on its negative half, and subtract the doubled second bundle. Add a complement of the second bundle pulled back from the base, so the resulting bundle is trivialized on the negative disk; collapsing that disk gives a reduced virtual bundle on the Thom quotient. Such a complement exists: finitely many local frames and a subordinate partition of unity embed a bundle in a finite trivial bundle, and its orthogonal complement supplies it. Different complements have a common stabilization, and changing the radius or boundary collar gives a homotopy. Conversely, pull a reduced bundle on the quotient back to the positive disk with its boundary trivialization. These operations are inverse after adding elementary triples: the negative half is precisely the trivialized summand removed in the collapse. Thus the ordinary compact triple character used here is [F2]'s relative character, and it respects pullback, extension by zero and products. For products the clutching construction gives tensor products of the resulting reduced virtual bundles; hence [F2]'s ring identity gives the relative product identity. [F1, F2, F6, F7, construct]

1.2 On $\Lambda^\bullet\mathbb C^r$ put $c(v)=\varepsilon_v-\varepsilon_v^*$ for real $v\in\mathbb C^r$. These are skew-adjoint Clifford matrices; for a unitary basis their two-dimensional factors are exactly the matrices in [F3]'s supplier, and their graded tensors span the full matrix algebra. The action $\Lambda^\bullet u$ of $u\in U(r)$ preserves grading and conjugates $c(v)$ to $c(uv)$. Choose either spin lift $s$ of the realification of $u$. The operator $(\Lambda^\bullet u)\rho(s)^{-1}$ commutes with every Clifford matrix, hence is a unit scalar $z$. Replacing $s$ by $-s$ replaces $z$ by $-z$, so $u\mapsto[s,z]\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(2r)$ is well-defined; local continuous lifts to the spin double cover show continuity, and multiplication of the implementing matrices proves it is a homomorphism. Thus the unitary frame bundle of $W$ induces a specified Spin-c lift whose associated spinor bundle is $\Lambda^\bullet W$. Its Clifford symbol is isomorphic as a relative triple to $D=\varepsilon_v+\varepsilon_v^*$: multiply degree $2j$ in the source by $(-1)^j$ and degree $2j+1$ in the target by $(-1)^j$; exterior multiplication is unchanged and contraction changes sign. In rank zero use the trivial lift and the even line. Therefore [F3] applies to the exact exterior symbol in [F1], with its plane map $z$ and its direct-sum product. [F1, F3, construct, algebra]

1.3 Choose a smooth embedding $f:F\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^N$ and its normal bundle $V$. Such an embedding can be constructed from finitely many coordinate charts and bump functions: take the vector of all functions $\phi_\alpha$ and $\phi_\alpha x_{\alpha,j}$, where the $\phi_\alpha$ are supported inside charts and their positive sets cover $F$. Equality of these vectors determines a common chart with $\phi_\alpha>0$ and then its coordinates, giving injectivity; differentiating the same coordinates shows injectivity of the derivative. Compactness makes it an embedding. An ambient metric splits $f^*T\mathbb R^N=TF\oplus V$ and embeds $T^*F$ into $T^*\mathbb R^N$ by zero normal covector. Its normal bundle, pulled back to $T^*F$, is $V\oplus V^*$: a connection splits horizontal and vertical tangent directions, and the two missing directions are the normal base vector and normal covector. Homotopies of the connection preserve this identification. At the zero section the cotangent symplectic form is the direct sum of the forms on $TF\oplus T^*F$ and $V\oplus V^*$; their symplectic orientations therefore multiply. Fiber dilation contracts $T^*F$ onto its zero section and preserves nondegeneracy, so the same orientation identity holds everywhere. [given, construct, algebra]

2.1 Let $L$ be a complex line, $x=c_1(L)$, $u_L$ its complex-oriented cohomological Thom class, and $\tau_L$ the plane-normalized Bott symbol [F3]. Thom isomorphism uniquely writes $\operatorname{ch}_c(\tau_L)=u_L A(L)$. The zero-section identity gives $x A(L)=1-e^x$. This equation alone cannot be divided by $x$ on an arbitrary base. Instead apply it to the tautological line on $\mathbb{CP}^k$: for each coefficient through degree $2k-2$, multiplication by $x$ is injective by [F4], so $A(\gamma)=(1-e^x)/x$ through that degree. For any prescribed finite degree choose the stage one degree higher. Compatibility under stage restriction determines every required coefficient, including the constant $-1$. A line on a finite CW base is pulled back from a sufficiently large finite stage of its classifying map, so naturality proves
$$\operatorname{ch}_c(\tau_L)=-u_L e^x\operatorname{Td}(L)^{-1}.$$
This also verifies the sign: on a complex-oriented plane the compact character of the prescribed Bott generator integrates to $-1$. [F2, F3, F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 For a rank-$r$ complex bundle $W$, pull to its flag splitting space. There $W=\bigoplus_jL_j$, and [F3], [F5] and the product identity in step 1.1 give
$$\operatorname{ch}_c(\tau_W)=(-1)^r u_W e^{c_1(W)}\operatorname{Td}(W)^{-1}.$$
Indeed multiplication of the line formulas gives the displayed factor, the sum of the line first Chern classes is $c_1(W)$, and the product of their Todd factors defines the Todd class. To descend, first write the left-hand side as $u_W A(W)$ by the ordinary Thom isomorphism. Pullback preserves $u_W$, and [F4]'s rational injectivity identifies the unique coefficient $A(W)$ with the displayed symmetric series. This proves the formula on the base, including rank zero. [F2, F3, F4, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Let $V$ be a real rank-$r$ metric bundle and identify its double $V\oplus V^*$ with $V_{\mathbb C}$ by $(v,\eta)\mapsto v+i\eta^\sharp$. The real structure identifies $V_{\mathbb C}$ with its complex conjugate. Consequently $2c_1(V_{\mathbb C})=0$ and $c_1(V_{\mathbb C})=0$ rationally. The complex orientation is $dv_1\wedge d\eta_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dv_r\wedge d\eta_r$, while the cotangent normal orientation is $d\eta_1\wedge dv_1\wedge\cdots\wedge d\eta_r\wedge dv_r$; their ratio is $(-1)^r$. If $u_-$ denotes the latter Thom class, step 3.1 therefore becomes
$$\operatorname{ch}_c(\tau_{V_{\mathbb C}})=u_-\operatorname{Td}(V_{\mathbb C})^{-1}.$$
All formulas are invariant under real orthogonal frame changes: their doubled real determinant is positive. Thus they apply without an orientation on $V$ or on its base. [F1, F5, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Form $j_!(a)$ by pulling $a$ to that normal bundle, multiplying by $\tau_{V_{\mathbb C}}$, and extending from a tubular neighborhood by zero. A tubular neighborhood exists here directly from the ambient Euclidean normal map: its derivative at the zero section is invertible; the inverse function theorem and compactness of the part of the zero section meeting the support give an injective sufficiently small neighborhood. Shrinking that neighborhood changes its collapse by a radial homotopy. Step 1.1 and step 4.1 give
$$\operatorname{ch}_c(j_!a)=j_*\bigl(\operatorname{ch}_c(a)\,\pi^*\operatorname{Td}(V_{\mathbb C})^{-1}\bigr),$$
where $j_*$ means multiplication by $u_-$ and extension by zero in ordinary compact-support cohomology. For the pairing in [F8], $\int j_*\alpha=\int\alpha$: subdivide a relative fundamental cycle subordinate to normal trivializing neighborhoods, and apply the relative cup-cap pairing on each product disk. The ordered normal Thom generator evaluates to $1$ on its normal disk by normalization, leaving the corresponding tangent coefficient; summing these coefficients gives the original pairing. The local generators of the total fundamental class are exactly these ordered products by step 1.3. Thus this is a cohomological fundamental-class pairing and requires no implicit de Rham comparison. This argument also works for virtual classes and for nonorientable $F$, since its cotangent orientation is global. [F2, F5, F8, step 1.1, step 1.3, step 4.1, construct]

6.1 By [F3], $K_c^0(T^*\mathbb R^N)$ is the infinite cyclic group generated by the $N$-fold plane Bott product, whose character integrates to $1$ with the $d\theta$ orientation: each factor has complex-oriented integral $-1$ by step 2.1, and reversing each of the $N$ plane orientations supplies another $(-1)^N$. Thus the integer coefficient of $j_!a$ in this generator is its integrated compact character. Since $TF_{\mathbb C}\oplus V_{\mathbb C}$ is trivial, multiplicativity of the Todd series gives $\operatorname{Td}(V_{\mathbb C})^{-1}=\operatorname{Td}(TF_{\mathbb C})$. Integrating step 5.1 proves the first formula for the ordinary class $a$. Its right-hand side uses no embedding or tubular data, so the integer defined by any such construction is independent of those choices. [F3, step 2.1, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 Put $H=\overline{\langle h\rangle}$ in the acting torus. Since $h$ fixes every point of $F$, continuity makes $H$ act trivially on $F$, hence on $T^*F$. On a compact disk-bundle representative each bundle has only finitely many $H$-weights. Here is a local justification of the finiteness assertion: in a unitary local frame the character is a continuous function of the base point, uniformly on the compact group $H$; its Fourier coefficients are the integer multiplicities of characters. Close base points have uniformly close characters and hence all multiplicities equal, because the coefficient differences have absolute value less than $1$. The weight list is locally constant and the disk has finitely many components. The weight projections are the integrals of the action against the conjugate characters, so are continuous projections of locally constant rank and define eigenbundles. Every equivariant symbol map preserves them. Direct sums, homotopies and elementary triples preserve the resulting weighted ordinary K-class, so $\operatorname{ch}_{h,c}$ is well-defined. Tensoring eigenbundles multiplies eigenvalues, and [F2] gives multiplicativity with an absolute bundle class. Weightwise application of step 6.1 proves the trace-weighted formula. Its degree-zero value on a bundle over a point is $\operatorname{tr}(h)$, whereas the ordinary Chern character's degree-zero value is its dimension; thus a degree-zero Borel rank cannot replace this operation. [F1, F2, step 6.1, construct, algebra]

8.1 On $F\subset M^g$, the fixed subspace of $dg$ is $TF$; the invariant metric gives an orthogonal splitting $TM|_F=TF\oplus\nu$ and no $1$-eigenvector in $\nu$. The exterior-power identity in [F1] gives the degree-zero term
$$\operatorname{ch}_g(e_g)_{[0]}=\det_{\mathbb C}(I-g|_{\nu_{\mathbb C}^*})=\det_{\mathbb R}(I-g|_\nu)>0.$$
In the finite-dimensional cohomology ring of $F$, all positive-degree classes are nilpotent. Writing $\operatorname{ch}_g(e_g)=c+u$ with $c$ the nonzero locally constant term, its inverse is the finite geometric sum $c^{-1}\sum_{k\ge0}(-u/c)^k$. Similarly a representation $s$ of nonzero character acts under step 7.1 as the invertible scalar $\chi_s(g)$, so both the weighted character and the weighted pushforward extend by division by this scalar to representation localization. For a localized K-class $b$ with $e_g b=i^*\sigma$, multiplicativity forces $\operatorname{ch}_{g,c}(b)=\operatorname{ch}_{g,c}(i^*\sigma)/\operatorname{ch}_g(e_g)$. Substitution in step 7.1 proves the second displayed formula whenever the localized quotient exists. In particular it applies to the quotient furnished by a separately proved K-localization theorem; no such theorem was used to prove this comparison. [F1, F2, step 7.1, algebra]

9.1 For an elliptic complex, let $s$ be its symbol differential at a nonzero real covector. Exactness implies that $s+s^*$ has zero kernel: its square is $ss^*+s^*s$, whose quadratic form is $\|su\|^2+\|s^*u\|^2$, and an element killed by both is an element of $\ker s$ orthogonal to $\operatorname{im}s=\ker s$. Thus its even-to-odd block is invertible and defines the same compact-support construction, with no Dirac or isolated-point restriction. A zero-dimensional $F$ has $T^*F=F$, positive point orientations and Todd class $1$, so the integral is the finite fiber trace sum. Finally $(-d\theta)^n=(-1)^n(d\theta)^n$, proving the stated change-of-convention factor. These observations include the empty manifold, zero symbols and rank-zero normals. AC has been used only through the listed topological suppliers and finite smooth bundle constructions. [A1, F1, step 7.1, step 8.1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

The ordinary Thom comparison and the trace weighting are proved here. To obtain an equivariant analytic fixed-component index theorem one still needs (i) an equivariant compact-support K-localization theorem giving the normal inverse and compatibility of the topological pushforward, and (ii) equality of the equivariant analytic index with that pushforward for general elliptic symbols. The ordinary Spin-c Thom theorem and a Dirac index formula alone do not prove (ii).

Gilkey uses $dx_1\wedge d\xi_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_n\wedge d\xi_n$ as the cotangent symplectic orientation in §4.4; the accompanying dimension sign is essential when converting to that convention. Heitsch's Theorem 2.1 displays $(-1)^n$ in its ordinary symbol formula. These source comparisons fix conventions; they are not premises replacing the Thom computation above.

## Statement

Assume AC. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ act smoothly on compact smooth manifolds without boundary. The compact-symbol triple group has a homomorphism

$$a_{T,M}:K^0_{T,c}(T^*M)\longrightarrow R(T)$$

which sends the symbol of an equivariant elliptic operator to its analytic kernel-minus-adjoint-kernel index, and sends the folded symbol of a first-order elliptic complex to its alternating cohomology representation. It is $R(T)$-linear and respects equivariant diffeomorphisms and restriction of the acting group.

Let $f:Y\hookrightarrow M$ be a smooth equivariant embedding of compact manifolds, with real invariant metric normal bundle $N$. Extend a covector on $Y$ by zero on $N$ to obtain $j:T^*Y\hookrightarrow T^*M$. Its normal bundle is $\pi_Y^*(N\oplus N^*)$, with complex structure $J(v,\eta)=(-\eta^\sharp,v^\flat)$. Define $j_!$ by pulling a symbol to this complex normal, taking its graded product with exterior multiplication by $v+i\eta^\sharp$ plus its adjoint on $\Lambda^\bullet N_{\mathbb C}$, and extending from a tubular neighborhood. Then, for every $c\in K^0_{T,c}(T^*Y)$,

$$a_{T,M}(j_!c)=a_{T,Y}(c).$$

This includes arbitrary symbol classes and real normal bundles, without a Dirac-type or fixed-point-dimension restriction.

For the trivial group, embed $Y$ into $\mathbb R^N$ and form the same doubled-normal extension $j_!c\in K_c^0(T^*\mathbb R^N)$. This group is generated by the plane Bott product with plane map $z=x+i\xi$. Its integer coefficient is denoted $p_{Y,!}(c)$. One has

$$a_{\{1\},Y}(c)=p_{Y,!}(c).$$

In particular that integer is independent of the embedding. If $g\in T$ fixes $Y$ pointwise, its action splits a symbol into finitely many $g$-eigenbundle classes $c_\lambda$ on each compact disk representative, and

$$\chi_{a_{T,Y}(c)}(g)=\sum_\lambda\lambda\,p_{Y,!}(c_\lambda).$$

Every identity extends to localization at the virtual representations whose character at $g$ is nonzero, by division by that character. No assertion of an index distribution for transversally elliptic symbols is made.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** Realize the symbols analytically, use a compact normal sphere bundle for the embedding, and compute its vertical index before applying controlled excision.

**Given:** The data and exact conventions in the Statement and [F1]–[F6].

1.1 Apply [F2] to a representative of a compact-support triple. Its continuous bundles and maps are smoothed, radially identified with base bundles, and represented by a homogeneous elliptic symbol by the proved constructions in that supplier. Every relation in the group of [F1] is preserved by [F2], so its additive index descends to $a_{T,M}$. Tensoring by representations proves $R(T)$-linearity. The same supplier proves the claimed operator and complex identifications, using matrix ellipticity and harmonic representatives. Its group restriction and diffeomorphism assertions give the stated naturality. In particular this step constructs an index on symbols; it does not assume an embedding theorem for that index. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 First consider the zero section of a real rank-$k$ equivariant metric bundle $N\to Y$. Its orthonormal frame bundle $P\to Y$ is a smooth principal right $O(k)$-bundle; $T$ acts on frames by the differential fiber action and commutes with right multiplication. Its compact normal sphere bundle is $Z=P\times_{O(k)}S(\mathbb R^k\oplus\mathbb R)$. It has an invariant open chart $P\times_{O(k)}\mathbb R^k=N$ around its north section. The vertical compact symbol is the $O(k)$-equivariant extension of $b_{\mathbb R^k}$ from this chart. By [F2] it has a smooth equivariant homogeneous realization, whose order may be changed to one without changing its class or index. Its finite-dimensional kernel $K$ and adjoint kernel $L$ obey $[K]-[L]=1$ by [F4]. Invariant orthogonal decompositions into irreducible finite-dimensional $O(k)$ modules then give an actual $O(k)$-equivariant isomorphism $K\cong L\oplus\mathbb C$: equality of their multiplicities is exactly this virtual equality. The fiber has trivial additional $T$ action, so the associated isomorphism is also $T$-equivariant. [F2, F3, F4, construct, algebra]

2.1 Represent $c$ by an order-one elliptic symbol on $Y$ using [F2], and apply [F3] to this base symbol and the vertical sphere symbol of step 1.2. The product index is the difference of the indices twisted by $K_P$ and $L_P$. Their equivariant bundle isomorphism $K_P\cong L_P\oplus\mathbb C_Y$, block additivity and quantization independence in [F2] make that difference exactly $a_{T,Y}(c)$. This statement concerns all symbol classes: a virtual difference of representatives is handled additively, and no differential or Dirac representative is required. [F2, F3, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 In a frame chart of $N$, split a covector on its total space into $(\alpha;v,\eta)$, with $\alpha\in T^*Y$ and $(v,\eta)$ the normal base and normal covector. The restriction of the associated product class from step 2.1 to $T^*N$ is the graded product of $c(\alpha)$ and the normal Koszul map at $v+i\eta^\sharp$. Its possible noninvertibility is the zero normal vector/covector over the compact support of $c$. The tensor differential contracts wherever either factor is invertible, so it has compact support. These local maps patch because real orthogonal frame changes intertwine exterior multiplication and its adjoint. A connection gives the indicated cotangent splitting; varying it is an affine homotopy, and [F3] proves the corresponding elliptic product-symbol homotopy. This is exactly the doubled-normal symbol defining the zero-section $j_!$ in [F1]. Thus the associated product is its extension from the normal open chart, rather than an unrelated symbol of the same dimension. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.2, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 For $f:Y\hookrightarrow M$, use [F5] to identify a disk neighborhood in $N$ equivariantly with a neighborhood of $Y$ in $M$. Fiber compression identifies the compact symbol in step 3.1 with one supported in this disk tube: over the compact support of $c$, choose one uniformly small normal radius, and compress the normal coordinates by a radial diffeomorphism. The same invariant open disk tube embeds in the compact sphere bundle $Z$ and in $M$. Its cotangent identifications have precisely normal complex structure $J(v,\eta)=(-\eta^\sharp,v^\flat)$; the differential of the tube map gives this along the zero section, and the connection splittings are joined by the homotopy just used. The controlled two-cutoff excision in [F2] identifies the kernel and adjoint-kernel representations of the extensions into $Z$ and $M$. Combining this equality with step 2.1 proves $a_{T,M}(j_!c)=a_{T,Y}(c)$. Normal ranks constant only componentwise cause no difficulty: compactness gives finitely many components, and apply the argument to each and add. For rank zero the tube is an open-and-closed component and the assertion is direct extension by zero; empty manifolds give zero. [F1, F2, F5, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 For the trivial group, construct an embedding $Y\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^N$ by finitely many chart functions: choose bump functions $\phi_i$ supported in coordinate charts whose positive sets cover $Y$, and map to the vector of all $\phi_i$ and $\phi_i x_{i,j}$. Equality determines a common positive chart and then its coordinates, proving injectivity; the same coordinate ratios show that the derivative is injective. Compactness makes it an embedding. Regard its target as the open Euclidean chart of $S^N$. Step 4.1 identifies the analytic index of $Y$ with the index of its doubled-normal extension to that sphere, and [F2] computes the latter in the Euclidean chart. By [F6], its class there is the integer $p_{Y,!}(c)$ times $b_{\mathbb R^N}$. The normalization [F4], restricted to the trivial group, sends this generator to $1$. Hence $a_{\{1\},Y}(c)=p_{Y,!}(c)$. The left-hand side is intrinsic, proving the asserted independence of embedding. This uses only ordinary Bott periodicity; no equivariant representation Bott isomorphism has been presumed. [F2, F4, F6, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

6.1 Suppose $g$ fixes $Y$ pointwise. The compact closure $H=\overline{\langle g\rangle}$ then fixes $Y$ and its cotangent bundle. On a compact disk representative, its unitary bundle representations have finitely many weights: character integration gives continuous projection operators onto each weight, whose ranks are locally constant. The finitely many weights spanning a fiber still exhaust its rank on a neighborhood; compactness gives a finite global list. Their projections split the bundles and preserve the symbol. Quantize the finite blocks separately and average over $H$. The resulting elliptic operator represents the restricted symbol, and its kernel and adjoint kernel split into the same weight blocks. Consequently its character at $g$ is $\sum_\lambda\lambda a_{\{1\},Y}(c_\lambda)$; quantization independence and group restriction in [F2] identify it with the character of $a_{T,Y}(c)$. Step 5.1 gives the stated formula with $p_{Y,!}$. Finally every index identity is $R(T)$-linear, and evaluation of $s\in R(T)$ at $g$ is a scalar. Localizing where $s(g)\ne0$ therefore extends the identities by ordinary division, proving the last assertion. [F2, step 1.1, step 5.1, construct, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

The comparison uses a compact normal sphere bundle and the proved associated-bundle product. Its analytic inputs include the explicit positive-order closure lift and controlled excision; ordinary Bott or a nonequivariant Dirac formula alone would not establish the embedding equality.

## Statement

Work in $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}$. Let a compact torus $T$ act smoothly on a compact smooth manifold $M$ without boundary, and let $F=M^T$. Then $F$ is a compact smooth embedded submanifold, its connected components $F_j$ are finite in number, and $T_pF=(T_pM)^T$ for every $p\in F$. If $F=\varnothing$, the component assertions are vacuous. The normal bundle $\nu_j$ of each component has no trivial $T$-representation in any fiber. Give $\nu_j$ a $T$-equivariant orientation, write $c_j=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb R}\nu_j$, and choose an invariant complex structure on it; let $\epsilon_j\in\{+1,-1\}$ compare that complex orientation with the chosen orientation. If the nonzero characters of the normal representation on a fiber, counted with multiplicity, are $\chi_{j,1},\ldots,\chi_{j,c_j/2}$, then the component of $e_T(\nu_j)$ in $H^0(F_j;\mathbb R)\otimes\mathcal R$ is

$$\epsilon_j\prod_{a=1}^{c_j/2}u_{\chi_{j,a}}.$$

Consequently $e_T(\nu_j)$ is invertible in $S^{-1}H_T^*(F_j;\mathbb R)$. When $c_j=0$, the product is empty, equals $1$, and the Euler class is already a unit.

## Proof

1.1 Average a Riemannian metric over normalized Haar measure on $T$. At $p\in F$, the exponential map of this invariant metric is $T$-equivariant and is injective on a sufficiently small ball in $T_pM$. Thus, for $v$ in that ball, $\exp_p(v)$ is fixed by every $t\in T$ exactly when $v$ is fixed by every linear map $d_pt$; the fixed set near $p$ is the exponential image of $(T_pM)^T$. Therefore $F$ is locally a smooth submanifold and $T_pF=(T_pM)^T$. The fixed locus is closed in compact $M$, hence compact; its connected components are open in this locally connected manifold and compactness gives only finitely many. [given, A1, A2, construct]

2.1 The orthogonal complement of $(T_pM)^T$ in $T_pM$ is the normal fiber, so it contains no $T$-fixed vector. The complexification of an orthogonal representation of the abelian group $T$ is a commuting family of unitary maps and decomposes into simultaneous character eigenspaces; complex conjugation pairs the $\chi$ and $\bar\chi$ spaces. A real one-dimensional character would have image in $\{+1,-1\}$ and is trivial because $T$ is connected. Thus every nontrivial real summand is two-dimensional. Averaging the fiber action against a character gives a smooth idempotent projection on the complexified normal bundle. Its rank is locally constant and hence constant on connected $F_j$. At one point only finitely many characters occur, since the fiber has finite dimension; constant ranks therefore imply exactly those finitely many characters occur everywhere on $F_j$. The real conjugate-pair subbundles are consequently smooth. [given, A1, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 If $\nu_j$ has nonzero weights, choose $X\in\mathfrak t$ outside the finite union of their kernels. For a character $\chi$, define the real linear weight $\omega_\chi(X)$ by $\chi(\exp(sX))=\exp(2\pi i s\omega_\chi(X))$. On its real weight subbundle the infinitesimal action $A_X$ satisfies $A_X^2=-(2\pi\omega_\chi(X))^2I$, so $J_\chi=A_X/(2\pi\omega_\chi(X))$ is invariant and satisfies $J_\chi^2=-I$. Their direct sum gives an invariant complex structure on $\nu_j$. Its complex orientation may agree or disagree with the chosen normal orientation, with comparison sign $\epsilon_j$. The weight projections vary continuously, so their ranks, and therefore the character multiplicities, are constant on connected $F_j$. If there are no weights, then $\nu_j=0$ and the complex structure is vacuous. [given, A1, A2, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 By step 1.1, $F_j$ is compact smooth, so [F2] applies. In local normal charts and Milnor principal charts the associated Borel normal bundle is an oriented rank-$c_j$ vector bundle over $BT\times F_j$; the pulled-back principal numeration, combined with a finite normal-bundle trivialization over compact $F_j$, supplies a numeration. Thus the general Thom theorem supplies its normalized real Thom class independently of any orientation of $M$. The torus acts trivially on $F_j$, hence $ET\times_TF_j\cong BT\times F_j$ and [F3] gives $H_T^*(F_j;\mathbb R)=H^*(F_j;\mathbb R)\otimes\mathcal R$. Restrict $e_T(\nu_j)$ to any point of $F_j$. The normal representation is the direct sum of the complex character lines in step 3.1; the Euler class of a direct sum is the product because the product of the normalized Thom classes restricts to the positive generator on each direct-sum fiber and hence is its normalized Thom class. By [F1] each line has Euler class $u_{\chi_{j,a}}$, and the orientation comparison gives $f_j=\epsilon_j\prod_a u_{\chi_{j,a}}$ as the degree-zero-in-$H^*(F_j)$ component. Every factor is nonzero and belongs to $S$, so $f_j$ is a unit in $S^{-1}\mathcal R$. [given, A1, F1, F2, F3, F5, step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Write $e_T(\nu_j)=f_j+n_j$, where $n_j$ has positive degree in $H^*(F_j;\mathbb R)$. By [F4], the ideal $\mathcal R\otimes H^{>0}(F_j;\mathbb R)$ has $N$th power zero for some $N\geq1$, hence $n_j^N=0$; this remains true after localization. In the localized ring the inverse is $f_j^{-1}\sum_{q=0}^{N-1}(-f_j^{-1}n_j)^q$, since multiplying by $f_j+n_j=f_j(1+f_j^{-1}n_j)$ telescopes to $1-(-f_j^{-1}n_j)^N=1$. If $c_j=0$, $n_j=0$ and $f_j=1$, giving the empty-product case as well. [given, A1, F3, F4, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume full AC. Fix integers $N\geq1$ and $k\geq0$ and a positive real stability parameter $\zeta$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ have their standard Hermitian structures. Define $\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N}$ to be the geometric quotient by $GL(V)$ of data $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I\in\operatorname{Hom}(W,V)$, $J\in\operatorname{Hom}(V,W)$, $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$, and $\operatorname{span}\{B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w):m\geq0,\ w\in W\}=V$. The positive parameter $\zeta$ specifies the positive-FI stability chamber. Let $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$, with rotation characters $t_1,t_2$ and dual framing characters $e_1,\ldots,e_N$. Thus $W$ has character $\mathbf W=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and $W^\vee$ has character $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$, where $h$ acts on $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$. Complexify the characters and work over the rational function field $K=\mathbb Q(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,a_1,\ldots,a_N)$, where $\epsilon_i=c_1^T(t_i)$ and $a_\alpha=c_1^T(e_\alpha)$.

For a partition $Y$, a Young diagram means a finite downward-closed subset of $\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2$; write $|Y|$ for its number of boxes. For an $N$-tuple $\vec Y=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N)$ set $|\vec Y|=\sum_\alpha|Y_\alpha|$, $\mathbf W=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$, $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$, and
$$\mathbf V_{\vec Y}=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha\sum_{(i,j)\in Y_\alpha}t_1^it_2^j.$$
Then $\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N}$ is smooth of complex dimension $2kN$, and its $T$-fixed points are isolated and in bijection with the $N$-tuples of partitions of total size $k$. At the fixed point $\vec Y$, the tangent character is
$$\operatorname{ch}_T(T_{\vec Y}\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N})=\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf V_{\vec Y}(t_1+t_2-1-t_1t_2)+\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf W^\vee+t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V_{\vec Y}.$$
For each character $\chi$, let $u_\chi=c_1^T(\chi)$. Let $E_{\vec Y}$ be the product of $u_\chi$ over the tangent weights counted with multiplicity; the fixed points are isolated, so none of these weights is zero. Define the fixed-point series by
$$Z^{\mathrm{fp}}_N(q)=\sum_{k\geq0}q^k\sum_{|\vec Y|=k}E_{\vec Y}^{-1}\in K\langle\!\langle q\rangle\!\rangle.$$
Each coefficient is a finite sum, and the series is formal; no analytic convergence is asserted.

If a $T$-equivariant isomorphism from the positive-FI quotient to the moduli of framed rank-$N$ torsion-free coherent sheaves on $\mathbb{CP}^2$ with Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$ is supplied, it transfers the fixed-point classification and tangent characters to that Gieseker space. The ordinary framed anti-self-dual moduli space is a separate zero-FI regular locus: identifying that locus with the regular ADHM quotient uses the separate ordinary dictionary below, and no fixed-point count or equality of series is asserted for it. If a separately proved noncompact equivariant pushforward for $\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N}$ has a localization identity with these isolated fixed points and tangent Euler classes, then its value on the unit is the coefficient displayed above. The compact ABBV formula alone does not establish such an identity: $\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N}$ is noncompact for $k>0$. This theorem makes no identification with an ordinary continuum gauge-theory path integral.

## Example

Assume full AC. Let $V=W=\mathbb C$, let $\zeta>0$, and let $T=(S^1)^2\times S^1$ have rotation characters $t_1,t_2$ and a framing-circle factor acting on $W$ in its defining representation. Write $h\in U(W)=S^1$ for a framing element; its character on $W$ is $e_1^{-1}$, and $e_1$ is the dual character. The action on ADHM data is
$$(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ).$$
Put $\epsilon_i=c_1^T(t_i)$ and $a_1=c_1^T(e_1)$, and work over $K=\mathbb Q(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,a_1)$ with algebraically independent generators. Let $\mathfrak M^\zeta_{1,1}$ be the quotient by $GL(V)$ of data satisfying $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$ and $\operatorname{span}\{B_1^{m_1}B_2^{m_2}I(W):m_1,m_2\geq0\}=V$, in the positive stability chamber, and let $q$ be the formal variable in the theorem's fixed-point series.

The datum $B_1=B_2=J=0$, $I=1$ is stable and satisfies the complex moment-map equation. The full-AC fixed-point theorem classifies the fixed points by one-color partitions; at total size one the unique tuple is $Y_1=\{(0,0)\}$. Its tangent character is $t_1+t_2$, with additive tangent weights $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2$. Define its tangent Euler product as the product of those additive weights, so $E_{Y_1}=\epsilon_1\epsilon_2$. The theorem's formal series $Z^{\mathrm{fp}}_1(q)$ has degree-$k$ coefficient $\sum_{|Y_1|=k}E_{Y_1}^{-1}$; hence the degree-one contribution is $(\epsilon_1\epsilon_2)^{-1}$.

$$t_1+t_2+\frac{e_2}{e_1}+t_1t_2\frac{e_1}{e_2}\qquad\text{and}\qquad t_1+t_2+\frac{e_1}{e_2}+t_1t_2\frac{e_2}{e_1}.$$
